title: Geography Guided Level 1 Sidecar v1
description: Map-first Guided Geography pilot for all Level 1 Geography cards.

source.name: Natural Earth
source.license: Public domain map data; StudyDeck SVG basemaps generated from Natural Earth GeoJSON.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem sits in Judea, west of the Jordan Valley.

questions.prompt: Which place is David's capital, the temple city, and the place where Jesus is crucified?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem is the capital city associated with David, the temple, and the crucifixion.

questions.prompt: David's capital and the temple city is ___.
questions.explanation: Jerusalem is the central city tied to David's kingdom and the temple.

lines: Jerusalem is the central city tied to David’s kingdom, the temple, and Jesus’ final week.
It sits in the hill country of Judea, west of the Jordan Valley.
Use Bethlehem, Jericho, Judea, and the Jordan River as nearby anchors.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Bethlehem?
questions.explanation: Bethlehem is just south of Jerusalem in Judea.

questions.prompt: Which small town is linked to David's family line and the birth of Jesus?
questions.explanation: Bethlehem is associated with David's family line and Jesus' birth.

questions.prompt: The small town linked to David's family line and Jesus' birth is ___.
questions.explanation: Bethlehem is the small Judean town tied to David and Jesus' birth.

lines: Bethlehem is a Judean town near Jerusalem.
It is remembered as David’s hometown and the birthplace of Jesus.
On the map, look just south of Jerusalem in the Judean hill country.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Mount Sinai?
questions.explanation: Mount Sinai is shown in the Sinai region between Egypt and the eastern Mediterranean world.

questions.prompt: Which mountain is where Moses meets God and receives the law?
questions.explanation: Mount Sinai is the covenant location associated with Moses and the law.

questions.prompt: Moses receives the law at Mount ___.
questions.explanation: Sinai is the mountain linked to Moses receiving the law.

lines: Mount Sinai belongs to the wilderness setting between Egypt and the promised land.
It is associated with covenant, law, and Israel’s formation after the exodus.
On the overview map, use Egypt and the Sinai Peninsula as the closest anchors.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks the Jordan River?
questions.explanation: The Jordan River runs through the Jordan Valley.

questions.prompt: Which river does Israel cross under Joshua, and where is Jesus baptized?
questions.explanation: The Jordan River is tied to Israel entering the land and to Jesus' baptism.

questions.prompt: Israel crosses the ___ River before entering the promised land.
questions.explanation: Joshua leads Israel across the Jordan River.

lines: The Jordan River runs through the Jordan Valley.
It marks key crossing, boundary, and baptism settings in biblical geography.
On the map, trace the river line between Galilee in the north and the Dead Sea in the south.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Jericho?
questions.explanation: Jericho sits near the Jordan Valley, east of Jerusalem.

questions.prompt: Which city has walls that fall after Israel marches around it for seven days?
questions.explanation: Jericho is the city linked to the falling walls story.

questions.prompt: The city whose walls fall after seven days of marching is ___.
questions.explanation: Jericho is remembered for its walls falling after Israel's march.

lines: Jericho sits in the Jordan Valley near the Jordan River.
It is remembered for Israel’s entry into the land and the story of the city walls.
On the map, look east of Jerusalem and close to the river valley.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Galilee?
questions.explanation: Galilee is the northern region on the inset map.

questions.prompt: Which northern region is tied to Jesus' upbringing and much of his public ministry?
questions.explanation: Galilee is the northern region where Jesus grew up and ministered.

questions.prompt: Jesus grows up and ministers much in the northern region of ___.
questions.explanation: Galilee is the northern region associated with Jesus' early life and ministry.

lines: Galilee is the northern region around Nazareth and the Sea of Galilee.
Many Gospel scenes happen in this region.
On the inset map, Galilee sits north of Judea and around the lake.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Nazareth?
questions.explanation: Nazareth sits in Galilee, north of Jerusalem and Bethlehem.

questions.prompt: Which town is where Jesus was raised?
questions.explanation: Nazareth is the town associated with Jesus' upbringing.

questions.prompt: Jesus is raised in the town of ___.
questions.explanation: Nazareth is the town where Jesus was raised.

lines: Nazareth is a town in Lower Galilee.
It is closely tied to Jesus’ upbringing.
On the Galilee map, look west of the Sea of Galilee.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks the Sea of Galilee?
questions.explanation: The Sea of Galilee is in the northern Galilee region.

questions.prompt: Which sea is linked to Jesus calming a storm and walking on water?
questions.explanation: The Sea of Galilee is the setting for several Gospel water stories.

questions.prompt: Jesus calms a storm on the Sea of ___.
questions.explanation: The Sea of Galilee is tied to the storm and walking-on-water accounts.

lines: The Sea of Galilee is the freshwater lake in the Galilee region.
Many Gospel stories happen around its shores.
On the map, use the lake shape as the main visual anchor.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Judea?
questions.explanation: Judea is the southern region centered on Jerusalem.

questions.prompt: Which southern region is centered on Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Judea is the southern region closely tied to Jerusalem and the temple.

questions.prompt: The southern region centered on Jerusalem is ___.
questions.explanation: Judea is the region centered on Jerusalem.

lines: Judea is the southern region around Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
It frames many events near the temple city and nearby wilderness.
On the inset map, Judea sits south of Galilee and west of the Dead Sea.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Damascus?
questions.explanation: Damascus is north of Israel in Syria.

questions.prompt: Which city is Saul traveling toward when his conversion vision occurs?
questions.explanation: Saul is on the road to Damascus when the conversion vision occurs.

questions.prompt: Saul is traveling toward ___ when his conversion vision occurs.
questions.explanation: Damascus is the destination in Saul's conversion account.

lines: Damascus is a major city north of the land of Israel.
It matters for travel routes and later New Testament events.
On the overview map, look north and east of Galilee.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Babylon?
questions.explanation: Babylon is placed in Mesopotamia, east of Syria and Israel.

questions.prompt: Which city becomes a major symbol of exile and imperial power?
questions.explanation: Babylon is closely tied to exile and imperial domination in the Bible.

questions.prompt: The city that symbolizes exile and imperial power is ___.
questions.explanation: Babylon becomes a symbol of exile and empire.

lines: Babylon sits far to the east in Mesopotamia.
It is tied to exile and imperial power in the biblical story.
On the overview map, it is much farther east than Damascus.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Egypt?
questions.explanation: Egypt is southwest of Israel and west of Sinai on the overview map.

questions.prompt: Which land is linked to Joseph, Israel's slavery, and the Exodus?
questions.explanation: Egypt is the land from which the Exodus story begins.

questions.prompt: The Exodus story begins from the land of ___.
questions.explanation: Egypt is the land Israel leaves in the Exodus.

lines: Egypt lies southwest of the land of Israel.
It is tied to refuge, slavery, exodus, and empire.
On the overview map, use the Nile and Sinai as nearby anchors.

questions.prompt: Which pin marks Rome?
questions.explanation: Rome is west of the eastern Mediterranean world, in Italy.

questions.prompt: Which imperial capital does Paul eventually reach as a prisoner?
questions.explanation: Rome is the imperial capital Paul eventually reaches as a prisoner.

questions.prompt: Paul eventually travels as a prisoner to ___.
questions.explanation: Rome is the political center Paul reaches near the end of Acts.

lines: Rome is far west of the eastern Mediterranean setting.
It represents imperial power in the New Testament world.
On the overview map, it sits across the Mediterranean from the Levant.
